content.title: About
content.content: Canned chicken soup 1906 is a ready‑to‑eat soup made from chicken meat, vegetables and spices, sealed in an airtight can. The sterilisation process preserves flavor and nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: First released in 1906 as a travel and expedition ration.
Aluminium can provides a long shelf life without added preservatives.
The chicken broth base contains collagen, giving the soup a rich taste.
1906 soup was widely used in military rations during World War I.
The original recipe used only natural spices, no artificial flavourings.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken meat supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and niacin, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Provides iron, phosphorus and potassium, important for blood formation and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Warm broth aids digestion, especially during colds.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The soup is mostly water, helping maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned soup often contains a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to chicken or added spices.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Aluminium cans may have trace BPA; choose BPA‑free labelled products when possible.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: While the original formula lacked them, modern versions may include stabilisers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup in a pot or microwave until boiling, stirring occasionally. You can add fresh vegetables, herbs or noodles for variety. Serve hot, optionally seasoned with black pepper.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.
